algorithm: Discounted cash-flow math: NPV by discounting, IRR by bisection on NPV(r)=0, DCF with Gordon terminal value, break-even by contribution margin, amortization by the standard loan formula.
complexity: O(T) per NPV/DCF over T periods; IRR bisection is O(T * iterations); amortization is O(months).
data_flow_ascii:
seeded inputs -> cashflows, loan terms, unit economics
cashflows -> npv(rate) -> present value
cashflows -> irr (bisection) -> discount rate where NPV=0
cashflows -> dcf_value -> enterprise value with terminal value
unit economics -> breakeven -> units to cover fixed costs
loan terms -> amortization_schedule -> monthly payment table
description_sentence: A financial modeler computing NPV, IRR by bisection, DCF valuation, break-even point, and a loan amortization schedule from seeded synthetic inputs.
failure_note: IRR raises a clear error when NPV has no sign change in the search range instead of returning a bogus rate.

functions.desc: Net present value of cashflows at the discount rate.
functions.name: npv

functions.desc: Internal rate of return via bisection on NPV(r) = 0.
functions.name: irr
functions.signature: irr(cashflows: list, lo: float = -0.9999, hi: float = 10.0, tol: float = 1e-6) -> float

functions.desc: DCF enterprise value with Gordon-growth terminal value.
functions.name: dcf_value
functions.signature: dcf_value(free_cash_flows: list, discount_rate: float, terminal_growth: float) -> float

functions.desc: Units needed for contribution margin to cover fixed costs.
functions.name: breakeven
functions.signature: breakeven(fixed_costs: float, price: float, variable_cost: float) -> float

functions.desc: Monthly payment split into interest, principal, and balance.
functions.name: amortization_schedule
functions.signature: amortization_schedule(principal: float, annual_rate: float, years: int) -> list

functions.desc: Seeded synthetic inputs: project cashflows, loan, unit economics.
functions.name: build_inputs

functions.desc: Build the command-line parser for the demo.
functions.name: build_parser

functions.desc: Entry point: seeded financial model demo.
functions.name: main

label: financial_model
output_shape: Prints the cashflow table with discount factors, NPV, IRR, DCF value, break-even units, and the amortization schedule.
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} that prices projects with NPV, IRR, and DCF and lays out loan payments month by month.

qa.a: It brackets the root where NPV changes sign and halves the interval until NPV is within tolerance, about 200 iterations max.
qa.q: How does the IRR bisection work?

qa.a: The final-year cash flow grows forever at the terminal rate; the Gordon formula values that perpetuity and discounts it to today.
Yes: npv, irr, dcf_value, breakeven, and amortization_schedule are pure functions of their inputs.

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} in Python implementing NPV, bisection-based IRR, DCF valuation, break-even, and amortization math.
run_notes: Discount rate, horizon, and loan terms come from the project params.
scaling_note: Closed-form math suits any horizon; portfolio-scale use would vectorize across many projects.
storage_note: No persistence: inputs and schedules are regenerated from the seed each run.
tradeoff_note: Deterministic formulas are auditable but ignore taxes, inflation, and risk beyond the discount rate.
